artefact_note: hashes cover the five generated artefacts; this report is not hashed into itself

gaps: the linkset carries the door graph's edges only: citation selectors, line ranges and lock hashes stay in the citation lockfile and the linked-data export — the sidecar is the relation index, not the citation record

W1.8 provenance labels (EXTRACTED / INFERRED / AMBIGUOUS) and confidences are not carried per link: RFC 9264's standard target attributes have no provenance slot, and inventing one would fork the format; the labels live on the linked-data export's EdgeAssertion nodes for the same edges

relations with no predicate in the closed vocabulary (today: exemplifies) are emitted under their wk: vocabulary URI as RFC 9264 extension relation types — typed, but with no external predicate semantics, which the report states
dangling targets are minted under the export's unresolved/ namespace so the link stays visible in the sidecar; the namespace names a non-target, not a fetchable resource

alignment.house: repo-relative path (checkpoints.d/<id>.json, evaluation/merkle-manifest.jsonl, a bag's payload paths)
alignment.notes: paths are the wiki's object identifiers; the linked-data export derives IRIs from them

alignment.house: checkpoint line_hash + signature; provenance manifest_sha256 and corpus_root in each checkpoint line; manifest-sha256.txt inside a bag
alignment.notes: sha256 throughout, as PREMIS records the algorithm with the digest

alignment.house: retention-policy.json classes (keep-forever vs clocked) and the witness copy outside the repo
alignment.notes: class-level only; no per-object preservationLevel is recorded — see gaps

alignment.house: <checkpoint id>/<event slug>, minted by this generator
alignment.notes: derived identifiers: stable because the source lines are hash-chained and immutable

alignment.house: derived from the register line kind + the act it records (creation / fixity check / replication / timestamp anchor)
alignment.notes: Library of Congress PREMIS event types where they fit; 'timestamp anchor' is a named local extension
the record's own datetime, never the generator's clock

alignment.house: anchor entries' recorded status, verbatim (a failed anchor stays failed); signature presence for checkpoint creation
alignment.notes: outcomes are copied, never upgraded — the schema's dual-anchor rule in PREMIS dress

alignment.house: signer identity on checkpoint lines (mehmed@llm-wiki); scripts/wiki_checkpoint.py for the acts the tool performs (anchoring, witness copy)
alignment.notes: the register records the identity string; agentType is not recorded there — see gaps

alignment.house: the checkpoint artefact / the provenance manifest the checkpoint binds
alignment.notes: every event also names its source register line by line_hash (the derivation audit trail, a house field riding beside PREMIS)

alignment.house: signer identity string; the checkpoint tool as software agent for its own acts
alignment.notes: no agent register exists; identity is the string on the signed lines

alignment.house: retention-policy.json classes (how long, what act an expiry names) + sensitivity.json classes (who may read/cite)
alignment.notes: policy-level mapping only: no per-object rights statements are recorded — see gaps

gaps: verification runs: evaluation/reverify-history.jsonl is an empty register (0 bytes) — no verification event exists on the record to align, so none is asserted here
erasures: evaluation/erasure-certificates.jsonl is an empty register (0 bytes) — no erasure event is asserted

bagging: scripts/wiki_bag.py (BagIt, RFC 8493) exists, but no bag artefact (bag-info.txt) stands in the tree, so no bagging event is asserted; the nightly Drive zip is a different route whose records live in goal state outside this tree and is likewise not asserted here
rights: the alignment maps retention + sensitivity CLASSES to PREMIS rights terms; no per-object rights statement is recorded anywhere in the wiki, so none is emitted

agents: the checkpoint register records the signer identity string only; PREMIS agentType (person / organization / software) is not on the record for the signer and is not invented here — only the tool's own acts name it, as software, by construction
preservationLevel is class-level (retention policy), never per-object, in the house records

not_covered: the capture -> ingest -> compile -> cite -> correct provenance chain is not serialised as PROV here: citation/claim provenance lives in the linked-data export (cito/oa terms, and prov:wasDerivedFrom for derives-from edges only), and the corrections ledger (wiki/rules/corrections-ledger.md) has no PROV serialisation
activity start and end are the same timestamp: the artefact records one date per commit
revision CONTENT is not carried: the bundle is metadata about revisions; the bytes are git's objects, and the artefact's latest_diff field is not reproduced
agents are the artefact's author strings, verbatim; no identity resolution beyond the string is asserted (e.g. two strings for one actor stay two agents)
renames: the artefact is built with git log --follow, so a renamed page's history is the followed history; the bundle asserts nothing about rename events themselves

a commit author string.prov: prov:Agent (the gateway author also prov:SoftwareAgent); rdfs:label and wk:authorString carry the string verbatim; the activity prov:wasAssociatedWith the agent and the revision prov:wasAttributedTo the agent
a commit author string.via: distinct author strings in the artefact

compiled page (a key of evaluation/page-.via: the page IRI the linked-data export mints

one recorded commit in a page's history.prov: prov:Activity, typed wk:RevisionActivity; prov:startedAtTime = prov:endedAtTime = the commit's recorded date; dcterms:description = the commit subject; wk:commit = the full sha

the page state a commit produced.prov: prov:Entity, typed wk:PageRevision; prov:wasGeneratedBy the activity; prov:specializationOf the page entity; prov:wasRevisionOf the previous (older) revision of the same page, where one is recorded; prov:generatedAtTime = the commit's recorded date
the page state a commit produced.via: one revision entity per history row

policy.default_rule: Every NEW internal identifier minted by wiki tooling from adoption forward is a UUIDv7, unless the object's register already runs a grandfathered scheme (below), in which case the register's own scheme continues — one scheme per register, never two in one register.
gaps: adoption is prospective and by convention: no existing tool is rewritten tonight to mint v7 — the first register that needs a new non-schemed identifier is where the default first applies, and that adoption is recorded when it happens

within one millisecond, string order among v7 ids is random-tail order, not insertion order (RFC 9562 makes the same statement); a register that needs intra-millisecond order keeps its own sequence field

grandfathered_schemes.disposition: continues; checkpoint ids stay sequential and human-citable

grandfathered_schemes.register: forecast ids cited across wiki pages

grandfathered_schemes.disposition: retained for WARC tooling interoperability; the ids are minted at capture time and stored in the WARC records themselves, not in a house register

minting_rules: time-ordered: the 48-bit unix millisecond field makes string order agree with mint order across milliseconds; identifiers sort by creation without a separate timestamp column
no re-minting: an identifier, once written to any register or artefact, is never replaced; a correction appends a new record naming the old id, it does not rewrite the id
legacy ids are never rewritten: grandfathered schemes keep issuing and resolving exactly as before; no migration, no alias table is created — each register remains the map for its own ids
an id names the object, not its content: content identity stays with the house hashes (citation lockfile line hashes, checkpoint line hashes, merkle roots), which this policy does not touch
mint through scripts/wiki_standards_bundles.py uuid7 new (or mint_uuid7 in this module) so the layout is the RFC's, verified against the RFC's own example vector in the test suite
out_of_scope: content hashes (sha256 lock hashes, merkle roots, canonical export hashes) are identifiers OF content and are not replaced by UUIDs
page paths and raw paths are the wiki's human identifiers and stay; the linked-data export's IRIs are derived from them, not from UUIDs
external identifiers (DOIs, ORCIDs, git SHAs, message ids from other systems) are recorded as issued, never re-minted
ephemeral protocol values minted at runtime (e.g. the multipart boundary in scripts/wiki_openrefine_trial.py) are not identifiers of record and are out of scope
